distinguishing_features: Passive interfacial-physics modification of the heat-transfer surface (SLIPS porous layer with infused liquid film) rather than a thermal cycling duty schedule on existing heaters
Failure-mode shift from adhesion-accumulation to shear-detachment via a low-adhesion liquid interlayer, versus tensile-stress-driven delamination/spallation from CTE mismatch
Eliminates scheduled thermal/shutdown intervention entirely, relying on fluid shear exceeding interfacial shear strength
Applied to crude preheat train asphaltene fouling specifically, versus carbon/coke fouling in reactor/furnace walls
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Prevent asphaltene fouling from adhering and hardening on heat-transfer surfaces so that recovery does not degrade between cleaning events, without requiring scheduled shutdowns or changing the operating schedule.
parsed.viable_reason: The infused low-surface-energy liquid layer cannot remain stable against a high-solubility asphaltene/alkane crude stream under tube shear and temperature; the SLIPS film would be displaced or diluted by the process stream (the very stream it claims to derive from), and the stated tau_int calculation uses inconsistent dimensions (G_a*gamma_sl/h_l does not yield Pa as claimed), so self-cleaning is not physically substantiated as written.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Neither prior art modifies the surface interfacial energy to convert the failure mode to shear-detachment; that departure is not an obvious routine extension of thermal-cycling or monitoring art, so the distinguishing mechanism itself is not obvious even though it fails feasibility.
